notes.title: Dustland Update v.0.1.9
notes.content:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/53b68b9f5eb0a6af09339e8d5500ebe782bdbb24.jpg"]In this patch, we focused heavily on optimization. Our main goal was to resolve the issue of ping spikes as player count increases—and along the way, we’ve touched and optimized many core game systems.


IMPROVEMENTS

1. New mechanic: Shelter Lifeline. You’ll now receive radio messages when a storm clears, when another player activates the elevator, or when Lesley is pleased with your mission progress.

2. Player limit on the map increased: 15 → 20.


TUNING & OPTIMIZATION

1. Fixed the issue with ping spikes. Ping should now remain significantly lower even with 5 or more players on the map.

2. Optimized all lootable items.

3. Optimized player character components.

4. Optimized the shooting system.

5. Partially reworked the marker system; events and event-related monsters are now displayed on the map.

6. Status effects (both positive and negative) are now shown in the HUD.

7. Updated the parameter widget in the character creation screen.

8. Optimized monster behavior logic.

9. The aiming reticle now automatically hides when interacting with NPCs.

10. A dedicated weapon tab has been added to the shop.


BUG FIXES

1. Fixed a bug where players could see each other’s markers on the map.

2. Fixed a bug that allowed multiple actions to be assigned to a single button.

3. Fixed a bug where hit marks appeared when shooting at corpses.

4.Fixed a bug that allowed players to bring items from the Tutorial into the Shelter by dropping and picking them up near the gate.



Thank you to everyone who stays with us and actively helps shape the project by sharing your feedback and comments. Together, we’ll keep making the game better!


Have a nice game!  

Best regards,  
Dustland team. 


 Dustland Discord

notes.title: Dustland Update v.0.1.8
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/7c358c5abd3b1d713a254e920296a64e4560ee72.png
Wanderers, welcome to the latest Dustland update!
This time, we’ve boosted optimization, increasing FPS by 15–20%, and introduced a brand-new mechanic: Memory Scraps. Explore the world to uncover fragments of the past!
We’ve also fixed bugs, enhanced locations, and added new sounds to make your journey even more immersive.

NEW FEATURES
1. Optimized all game locations. In the Tutorial, the Shelter, and in the wasteland, the average FPS has increased by 15–20%.
2. New mechanics: Memory Scraps:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/7220bc8b37becfa791c5d307fcc3aca18e3f0d08.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/db8932c197a1ac929bed8e59a00f4780837aca98.png
By interacting with otherworldly entities, you can glimpse fragments of events from before and during the cataclysm.
These visions feature the authors of the notes found in Dustland, along with familiar characters from the Shelter.
This update introduces 5 Memory Scraps. One can be found on the first floor of the SPTV television studio—the rest are yours to discover.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/e0f7809a039614b2af0ffece47355c1589170f94.gif
New Memory Scraps will be added in future patches and updates.

FINE-TUNING
[expand type=details expanded=false]1. Updated text tip style: keywords are now highlighted in color for better readability.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/256eea244dde4143c155cabc5600704f729f5af6.png
2. Added objects to the Tutorial that mark monster zones.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/9acefc0f7b941064dfa11a893f448c358c1ee775.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/e7f9e6d56a79de5508335d473181dfbf020cf1ac.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/34827e4fdb266f96e9eee530d7e15f37de3b184e.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/9e47d636aa43088289b711eacea6386d890ff972.png
3. Reworked and improved various locations on the map.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/533540f9035a3f022b8a84aba21ec7cce7594d32.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/6c59d1921c2402ad05c07deb130e9fa7baaf19b5.jpg
4. Sounds made by Oscars are now twice as loud, with an increased radius.
5. Added interaction sounds for training tablets.
6. Added new sounds for the character parameters widget.
7. Added sound effects for the water tank in the Shelter.
8. Added a sound cue for the scroll widget.
9. Added a box-opening sound for pneumatic tubes packages purchased with flasks.
10. Optimized character parameter replication for better performance.[/expand]

BUG FIXES
[expand type=details expanded=false]1. Removed visual artifacts (black squares on the landscape).
2. Fixed map locations where Dryers could get stuck waist-deep in the ground.
3. Completely fixed an issue where, when moving between locations, all armor except the helmet would sometimes not display. (We previously addressed this, but it persisted under unstable connections).
4. Fixed animation issues for Lesley.
5. Fixed collision issues for various objects on the map.
6. Fixed a bug where the respawn button in the Tutorial sometimes did not work on the first attempt.[/expand]

Enjoy the game! 

Sincerely, 
The Dustland Team.


Dustland Discord

notes.title: Dustland Update v.0.1.7
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/498964ba8664605d70126e7ac2cffa17195704b3.png

Wanderers, welcome to the updated Dustland! 
A lot of big changes and exciting improvements are coming your way!
In this update, we've refactored parameters, improved their display in the interface, added support for ultra-wide monitors, fixed visual artifacts on Radeon graphics processors, made further adjustments to monster behavior, and much more.

NEW FEATURES:
1. Character parameters refactored: All stats and bonuses now show more stable performance and are bug-free.
[expand type=details expanded=false]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/65e98eceaf47a16dada77ec4139d1e5fa428065f.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/709b56d918ff33eb43d99ee664fa4ff7f4c1eb1a.png[/expand]
2. Character parameters widget overhauled: A new “Open Full Stats” button has been added, allowing you to take a closer look at the character’s stats. For example, you can now see that Luck reduces fall damage and increases the chance of finding Bolts in containers.
[expand type=details expanded=false]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/6c2085bd180ff4ccdf9df4a26443b90fc2713a40.png[/expand]
3. Monster AI improved: Monsters can now lose sight of players and start searching for them from the last known location.
4. Russian voice-over added: Voice acting has been implemented for characters and narrative screens.
5. 10 new missions added:

 To Hell And Back I
 To Hell And Back II
 One Step To Insanity
 Only To The Worthy
 Grounded Flight
 The Citadel
 Love, Death & Kittens
 The Day the Thunder Struck
 Line of Communication
 Treasure Washed in Sand and Blood
These missions are challenging and intended for experienced players.
6. New items added: Saltglare Shards can now be found in containers or drop from defeated monsters. These shards hint at an upcoming new region and will play a role in future game mechanics.

FINE-TUNING:
[expand type=details expanded=false]1. If a player exits and re-enters the game during the Tutorial, they will now spawn at the last checkpoint instead of starting from the beginning of the level.
2. Monsters will no longer attack players under the effect of invulnerability.
3. The Terminal now plays a tutorial video when greeting players in the Shelter.
4. Unnecessary log messages that were overloading the server during shooting have been removed.
5. Auto-saves have been optimized by removing unnecessary save-related variables that were putting strain on the server.
6. The delay when equipping armor has been removed.
7. After completing the elevator tutorial, another mission will be given to interact with Lesley.
8. Updated map art: new points of interest, including the Portal, have been added to the map.
9. Monsters now return to their spawn point if they lose sight of their target or move more than 35 meters from where they spawned.
10. Monsters now return to their general spawn location, not a specific point.
11. Monsters now respond differently to movement sounds depending on whether the player is walking, running, or crouching.
12. Added sounds for placing items into containers, backpacks, and the Storage.
13. Added sounds for pumps.
14. Added sounds for Obelisks.
15. Added sounds for equipping armor and weapons.
16. Added sounds for buttons on the top panels.
17. Added sounds for the Pneumatic Mail.
18. Added sounds when opening loot containers.
19. Added sounds for the weapon window.
20. The character’s body now disappears 30 seconds after pressing “Respawn”, giving the player more time to use the syringe.
21. Improved backgrounds and art for events, the character window, and other UI screens.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/7bff1f94a0cef8fad5840fdc2eacc6a0e2658d6f.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/e7440b4e7f4db792d3f8844aba1260fdd9ddbc14.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/097e452ed6bba4670b867c5c5f1c324b45f52d39.png
22. The default small icons for quests have been replaced.
23. An explanatory text has been added to the character creation screen, showing that the character can be zoomed in and out using  the mouse wheel.
24. For optimization purposes, the detail distance for loot containers has been reduced.
25. Axe damage now depends on the body part hit and can be reduced by armor.
26. An idle animation has been added for the axe.
27. Some voice lines will be reworked in the near future.[/expand]

BUG FIXES:
[expand type=details expanded=false]1. Fixed a bug where female characters could make sounds with a male voice.
2. Fixed a bug causing FPS drops when opening the menu using the Esc key in the Tutorial, Shelter, or wasteland.
3. Fixed an issue where all windows were stretched when playing on ultra-wide monitors.
4. Fixed a bug that caused visual artifacts when playing on computers with Radeon graphics cards.
5. Fixed a bug that caused shooting to work incorrectly when a different weapon was placed in the axe’s special slot.
6. Fixed a bug that sometimes prevented a mission from being selected when pressing “Accept” in the mission selection window.
7. Fixed a bug where monsters sometimes didn’t produce sounds.
8. Fixed a bug where characters’ black skin would take on a purple hue in the Shelter.
9. Fixed issues with the visualization of seams between parts of neutral armor.
10. Fixed a bug that caused the widget with the scrollbar to extend beyond the screen when selling items to the merchant.
11. Fixed a bug where an item would be dropped on the ground when Shift+LMB was pressed on it in the character window.
12. Fixed a bug that caused the server to crash when the player exited to the main menu after dying while affected by a status effect.
13. Fixed a bug that caused Dryer corpses to produce sounds.
14. Fixed various bugs related to screen resolution settings.
15. Fixed a bug where the Stimulant and the Flask of Tea with Salt lasted longer than the specified time.
16. Fixed a bug where, in rare cases, the character could still turn over after performing parkour.
17. Fixed a bug where pressing the B button before the character was fully loaded would crash the game.
18. Removed the rudimentary ability to right-click on an equipped weapon.
19.Fixed a bug where the character wouldn’t make a sound when taking poison damage.
20. Temporarily LMB axe attacks no longer come with a slight forward movement.
21. Added missing localization. 
22. Fixed animation issues with Lesley.[/expand]

BALANCE CHANGES:
We discovered that firearm damage was being calculated incorrectly, so we’ve rebalanced the damage for all weapons. Details below.

Weapon damage changes:
Revolver

 Common: 25 → 30
 Rare: 25 → 31
 Epic: 25 → 33
 Legendary: 28 → 33
SMG

 Common: 15 → 20
 Rare: 15 → 20
 Epic: 15 → 22
 Legendary: 16 → 25
Automatic Rifle

 Common: 20 → 25
 Rare: 20 → 26
 Epic: 20 → 27
 Legendary: 22 → 30
Sniper Rifle 

 Common: 36 → 45
 Rare: 35 → 42
 Epic: 37 → 50
 Legendary: 40 → 65
2. The drop rate for legendary weapons from military crates has been reduced from 2.36% to 0.62%.

These aren’t all the changes we’ve been working on since the last patch. We’ve made a lot of fixes on the main map, achieved FPS improvements across all game locations, and also completed work on new mechanics that will provide a deeper look into Dustland’s lore. All of this will be available in the update next week!


Enjoy the game! 

Sincerely, 
The Dustland Team.


Dustland Discord

notes.title: Dustland Update v.0.1.6
notes.content:
Wanderers, welcome to the latest update for Dustland! It includes fixes, balance changes, improvements, and a brand-new Portal Echo event. Learn about the changes, gear up, and venture into the unpredictable and dangerous wasteland!

IMPROVEMENTS (NEW)
[olist]
 New mechanic: Three Disguises.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/9983454827a8ced2209d5af0b26374423c9a6ada.png
 Three enigmatic masks have appeared in the Mysterious Room within Shelter, each can be upgraded using Insight Points. Each disguise offers the player a substantial bonus but also applies a debuff.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/73a3438ebddb02797d854f18b0154fc65b983cce.gif
 New mechanic: the Portal Echo event. We are introducing regular events in the game, with start times synchronized to server time. The first of these events will be Portal Echo, where you must defeat all monsters within the allotted time to earn rewards. Tackling this task alone will be challenging; so team up with other players on the map to increase your chances of success. Once you win, it's up to you to decide whether to share the reward with your teammates or keep it all for yourself.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/f92f556672c5fa45e59412d3d5e302a49f8a16bb.png
 An Events tab has been added to the main menu, where you can view details about current and upcoming events.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/ad3232544d7ee4db5faacda82f1bda156cc152c1.png
 You can no longer die in the Shelter—players inside are granted a permanent invulnerability buff.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/bf802473afd6b2828c731f3cb7f30114b9cfcfcd.png
[/olist]

FINE-TUNING
[olist]
 Added a smooth transition between walking, jogging, and sprinting. The player now picks up speed gradually.
 Added a training tablet for social mechanics (squad, voice, and text chat).
 Updated the videos for the tablets explaining Insight Points and Artifacts.
 Added a tutorial quest for using the Three Disguises feature.
 The tutorial quest for using Artifacts now also takes the player to the room with tablets.
 The volume of elevator sounds has been increased. They can now be heard from up to 50 meters away.
 The visual effect of overheating now increases gradually, reaching its peak at a body temperature of 50 degrees.
 Added several new directional signs throughout the Shelter.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/989c0e4fac1a97492c257aa08c1a489358064fbe.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/98137ee313b69f80c060478ad05222cb123504d5.png
[/olist]

BUG FIXES
[olist]
 Fixed a bug that caused the character to assume an unnatural position after parkouring on surfaces with complex geometry.
 Fixed a bug that caused the camera to jerk when changing movement speed.
 Fixed a bug that prevented the player from replenishing water from the Tank when they had 100+ water.
 Fixed a bug that caused the merchant interface to disappear when pressing the Q button.
[/olist]

BALANCE CHANGES
[olist]
 Quests that involve using the syringe: the reward has been increased by approximately 50%.
 Artifacts with a chance to apply poisoning and bleeding effects: the probability of triggering has been increased from 2–3% to 4–5%.
 Tar of Tea with Salt: weight increased from 0.2 to 0.3, and effect reduced from 99% to 45%.
[/olist]

Thanks for your feedback!

Your input, ideas, and enthusiasm help us make the game better! Stay tuned—there's more to come. See you in the wasteland!

Have a nice game!

Best regards,
Dustland team.

Dustland Discord

notes.title: Dustland Update v.0.1.4
notes.content:
Players, welcome to the latest update for Dustland! This patch brings improvements, fixes, and balance adjustments to make your journey through the grim wastelands more enjoyable. Let’s take a look at the key changes!

IMPROVEMENTS (NEW)
[olist]
 A new room has been added to the Shelter where you can learn about most of the game mechanics.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/21655f33e9b0d5848c7d407fea1b7d9fd0ede45a.png
 You can now take shelter indoors during storms.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/9abe996c581868300cb604bcb4578c9f3049a67c.jpg
 Invulnerability has been added for players after they spawn on the map. You will now be invulnerable until you take an action or until the invulnerability timer runs out.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/d763e39a75c396b25e186246c14c7e21e557fb93.png
 The order in which quests become available has been changed. Lesley now first offers the tutorial quest on how to use the elevator, and only after completing it will the other quests, including the main story quest, become available.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/2d00180eff19dfba415ac75cc737322f94c3a16a.png
 Quests can now affect where you will spawn on the map. This aims to provide smoother immersion and improve gameplay. This mechanic has been applied to quests such as Dustland: Introduction and Elevator Operation Check.
[/olist]

FINE-TUNING
[olist]
 Updated the Artifacts window.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/0c74a3f540b58ef36ec8dfdbf550f71bbbc1300d.png
 Updated the logic of monster states. This is an important step in improving them, with more improvements to follow. In this patch, monsters’ behavior will be more stable, and it will be easier to escape from them.
 In the Shelter, the passageways to the Mystical Room and Ammar’s Room have been widened.
 The quest system has been refactored aiming to ensure more reliable performance and address issues with rare server crashes and save file corruption.
 Fixed the location of player spawn points, placing some of them farther from monsters spawn points.
 Updated the sounds for the Draynes.
 Added sounds for syringe usage.
 Added missing parkour sounds.
 Added sounds for jumping and landing with weapons.
 Added a sound when completing a quest stage.
 Added a sound for using the gate in the Shelter and in the Tutorial.
 Added sound effects for opening and closing the quick access panel.
 Added a sound for opening burial urns.
 Added a sound for using consumables.
 The Connecting to the server screen has been replaced with the standard loading screen.
 Quick access slots now show item quantity.
 Most button tooltips now adapt to the assigned functions of the buttons.
 Added visual effects to bring more life to the map.
 The F1 button tooltip has been moved under the container widget.
 Updated effect icons.
 A note has been added to all quests that do not place markers on the map.
 Added a sound for revealing a part of the painting.
[/olist]

BUG FIXES
[olist]
 Fixed a bug where completed quests and quests abandoned by the player would not be returned to the quest pool.
 Fixed a bug where it was sometimes impossible to interact with the backpack of a killed player or the Wanderer.
 Fixed a bug where movement sounds were not heard when holding a revolver.
 Fixed a bug where the character would jump when switching from running to crouching, which happened if movement speed exceeded the default speed.
 Fixed a bug where ??? monsters could get stuck in an infinite loop of the same animation.
 Fixed a bug where Oscar monsters could slide along the ground while attacking or disappear.
 Changed the location of some Oscar monster spawn points and fixed a bug that caused them to appear on top of the pipes at the airport.
 Fixed a bug that prevented the animation for using a consumable when holding an axe.
 Fixed a bug that prevented the recovery of the normal movement speed immediately after the character was no longer encumbered.
 Fixed a bug that caused the interaction widget to remain on the screen after interacting with an NPC.
 Temporarily disabled The Meeting Place Cannot Be Changed quest.
 Fixed some visual bugs on the map.
 Fixed some collision issues on the map.
 Fixed a bug that prevented the book from being taken away from the player during the Comrade Lesley quest.
 Fixed a bug that caused the character to slide along the ground when holding down the Space key.
 Improved NPC performance in the Shelter by optimizing their code.
 Fixed a bug that allowed squads of more than four people.
 Fixed a bug that allowed two different types of poison ammo to exist in the game.
 Fixed a Russian localization error in the Can Anyone Hear Us? quest.
[/olist]

BALANCE CHANGES
Scorpion speed reduced from 600 to 500.
Scorpion hearing range reduced from 10,000 to 5,000.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/80996b2bc34daa0ca74d0918bf80c21f3496c78e.png

Thanks for your feedback!

This update is made possible by the ongoing support of our community. We have carefully reviewed your feedback and suggestions to make Dustland better. Please keep sharing your ideas and reporting issues—your feedback is incredibly important to us!

Have a nice game! 

Best regards, 
Dustland team.

Dustland Discord

notes.title: The Three Factions of Dustland
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/578121ff3621d40beddaa28ab9586668632b7def.png
Survivors!

From the character creation screen to a rusty box in an abandoned building out in the Wasteland, you’ve seen the names of the three main Dustland factions—the Marauders, the Murens, and the Tyrants. But who are they? What are their goals? Let’s find out.
[hr][/hr]
Faction Basics
The cataclysm that left the land barren of anything but sand and monsters forced human survivors to team up. People started to organize themselves into groups based on their previous professional skills and specializations. Each group used their experience to survive and achieve their objectives. But now, people join factions not for their ideals, but to survive yet another scorching day, settle into the Shelter, and then pursue their own personal goals.

Core Values and Beliefs
Marauders
Founded by people who, in some unfathomable way, survived the great storm beyond the Shelter. To this day, they guard their secrets.
They know the wasteland better than anyone. Veterans often venture into neighboring regions, bringing back their spoils.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/2d8cd59579b663b228406ae81cbfbc18955a941e.png

Murens
The personal faction of engineers who built the Shelter. The creators of the 'Ark' know its every corner and immediately gained power and influence when the cataclysm struck.
Now, the engineers themselves rarely leave the Shelter. Instead, they have others do all the work on their behalf. There is always some mystery to their actions and true intentions.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/72c1923c0792eba95a2eaf7b5b7093b32f582c45.png

Tyrants 
Police officers, port workers, blue collars, firefighters. The working class and those who had physical strength and access to firepower. They quickly banded together into a single faction.
They are marked by their toughness, roughness, and aggression. They control the Shelter’s entire stockpile of weapons.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/97e064d07f87a4ef83065f4151bf8eb3239533f3.png
“I like Tyrants — the horns on their helmets. Well, come on, who doesn't like horns?”
— Iskander, Dustland Developer
Primary Goals
The general objective for everyone and every faction is to survive and to figure out what caused the cataclysm. But there seems to be a silent mastermind lurking in the shadows and pulling the strings.

 Marauders : Survival, exploring the wasteland, discovering new territories.
 Murens: Maintaining the Shelter and studying the consequences of the cataclysm.
 Tyrants : Keeping control over the wasteland and claiming back territories.
Allies and Rivals
No one knows who heads the factions. They say their leaders have long gone crazy. But it’s not entirely true—at least not for the Murens. The factions operate independently of one another, but their interests constantly overlap, leading to unexpected alliances or conflicts.
Lesley (the quest giver) belongs to the Tyrant faction but assigns missions to all of the Shelter’s inhabitants. At times, it feels like he's deliberately pitting the factions against each other.
In the Shelter, people are not hostile to each other. In the Dustland, however, everyone is on their own. Even someone from your own faction can be dangerous. Or even someone from your squad. Always keeps you on edge, doesn’t it?

While faction members mostly work alone, they can work together to achieve their Seasonal Goal. It’s a global faction quest that faction members must complete together. As factions’ goals constantly collide, succeeding in your faction’s goal means preventing other factions from completing theirs.
[hr][/hr]
Gameplay Style and Strengths
Recommended Play Style

 Marauders : Stealth. Their armor is quieter, nimbler, and more inconspicuous. They can travel distances faster and remain unnoticed.
 Murens: Resource gathering. They are able to stay in the wasteland longer than others and carry more water to withstand the heat. While they can stay out longer, exploring locations as Murens is more challenging.
 Tyrants : Combat. They are a bit slower, but well armored and equipped. They are more of a fight rather than flight type of guys.Each faction has its own special set of armour.

Signature Abilities
These features, along with some others, will be added in future updates.

 Marauders : They can sell the loot they bring from the wasteland for more bolts than others.
 Murens: Water, the most valuable resource in the wasteland, is cheaper for them in the Shelter.
 Tyrants : They get a special deal on weapons in the Shelter: a better choice for a smaller price.
Water is the most important resource. Wanderers can gather it in the wasteland or buy it in the Shelter. But there are many other useful consumables, and you can always look for better weapons and armor.

Territorial Control
At the moment, there’s no territorial control in the game, but as the story progresses, we will add this element to the game.
[hr][/hr]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Now, you know who you’re dealing with. So, which faction will you choose?
[hr][/hr]
Keep hydrated and we’ll see you in Dustland!

Dustland Discord

notes.title: December 24th Patch Notes
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/9d1df74bdf848581a0183a0804132d8917cfb1fe.png
Dustlanders!

In this patch, we’ve promptly addressed some of the issues and bugs that you helped us identify. Additionally, we’ve implemented several improvements to enhance your gameplay experience.
Thank you to everyone who shared feedback and engaged with us on Discord and Steam! We remain committed to improving the game. Early Access is a crucial phase, where your input helps us refine the game with every update.
[hr][/hr]
Improvements

 Inventory Log: Items now display their name and quantity when added to your inventory.
 Streamlined Login: After account creation, you’ll be directed straight to the main menu, skipping the login screen.
 Account Restrictions:
 Creating multiple accounts on the same Steam profile is no longer possible.
 Logging into your game account from another Steam profile has been disabled.
These changes aim to prevent save file corruption and login issues.

If you encounter login problems after the update, feel free to contact us at report@redpad.games or via Discord.

Tunings

 Storm Behavior: Monsters now stop attacking and scatter during storms.
 Mystical Room Tutorial: Added a new tutorial step in the Shelter to introduce players to the Mystical Room.
 Pump Status: Interacting with an empty pump now triggers a notification about its current fill level.
 Training Completion: The final step of the tutorial quest in the Shelter now clearly indicates the end of training.
 Elevator Tutorial: Added a new quest to help players learn how to use elevators and remember their locations.
 Quest Limits: The quest selection screen now displays the maximum number of active quests you can have.
 Dialog Navigation: Added a prompt showing that dialogs can be scrolled with the left mouse button.
 Elevator Sounds: Elevators now feature sound effects.
 Shelter Navigation: Added directional signs to make navigation easier in the Shelter.
 Monster Disengagement: If a player moves out of reach, certain monsters will stop chasing them.


Bug Fixes

 Fixed an issue where jumping on another player’s or a monster’s head could cause you to be launched into the air.
 The map (M) no longer stutters and scales correctly.
 The quest widget now works as intended; if it still malfunctions, pressing L will reset it.
 Ambient sounds have been added to both the Map and the Tutorial.
 Loading screens now properly display Russian localization.
 Fixed issues with syringe animations breaking during use.
 Smoke above urns now reliably indicates whether they contain items.
 Monsters labeled "???" no longer get stuck halfway into the ground.
 Opening interface windows during character loading in the Shelter no longer causes crashes.
 Player replicas on the map now persist for 30 seconds instead of disappearing after 5.
 Mouse sensitivity sliders now function correctly and stay within the window boundaries.
 Insight points can no longer be earned by canceling quests.
 The friends list window now closes properly.
 Correct information is now displayed in the widget text for completed or failed Obelisk challenges.
 Several collision issues on the Map have been partially fixed.
 Some visual glitches on the Map have been addressed.
 Fixed a visual bug where characters’ heads were visible under helmets.
 Resolved a rare crash related to the merchant when transitioning via elevator.
 The crosshair now functions correctly in windowed mode and on unconventional monitor setups.
 The Wanderer reliably spawns on the map as intended.
 Falling into a portal no longer causes players to get stuck — it now behaves as expected.
[hr][/hr]
Important: there will be a new login system upgrade in the patch, so you will have to re-enter your email and password once upon first login.

If you forget your password, reset it from the log-in window. If you forget both your email and password that you used to create your account, please send us your SteamID – we'll try to restore your account.
[hr][/hr]
See you in the Shelter!

notes.title: Early Access release on December 9th
notes.content:
Dustlanders!

We’ve come a long way and have reached an amazing milestone:
The game is finally out in Early Access!

We’ve worked hard to get Dustland to this point, and it wouldn’t be possible without you, the players. You are an integral part of this process and will continue to be as we move forward. 

That being said, it’s important we understand that Early Access is still a work in progress. There will be bugs, glitches, various technical issues — you name it. If you see an issue that impacts your gameplay, report those nasty bugs as soon as possible, so we address them in a timely manner. Don’t hesitate to reach out, join our Discord, and leave reviews — they don’t go unnoticed!


What has been done since the last PT
Since the last PT we’ve fixed the following issues:


 Updated death and loading screens.
 Windows now close with the same button they open with.
 Items in the store are now sorted from top to bottom by rarity. Keycards and ammo are always at the top.
 Light axe attack speed has been increased.
 Fixed the character ragdoll; it no longer spins after death.
 Updated the support screen with an email address where players can write to.
 Drains no longer pass through the player when attacking.
 Added VFX disappearance to the burial urn if it was recently opened and has no bolts left.
 The inventory now opens with the I key, friends with P, and items on the ground with G (inventory, party, ground).
 The Axe tutorial quest has been replaced with a revolver quest. Added a description that killing drains is not mandatory.
 The duration of most consumables has been increased from 15 to 60 seconds.
 Added the ability to rotate the camera while using the syringe. The syringe can now be interrupted not only by opening the interface.


Bug Fixes:

 Fixed a bug where the weapon in the player’s hands would disappear.
 Fixed a bug where the ritual would give non-functional weapons.
 Fixed a bug where no more than 2 players could leave in the elevator. Now, everyone who fits can leave.
 Fixed a bug where the Oscar monster would disappear if it couldn’t reach the player.
 Fixed a bug with quests that could cause the Training server to crash.


Locations:

 Faction banners have been added to the map.
 The hub has been updated (the merchant and their table, pneumatic mail, added a sign for the water tank, collision fixes).
 The weather phenomena institute has been improved.
 Fixed some collisions on the map.
 Reduced the number of monsters near the first storyline quest.



A big thanks to everyone who contributed to Dustland during the closed Beta stage, you’re the GOAT! By the way, remember the raffle announced here? The winners have been randomly chosen and have received their permanent EA access codes to their email addresses (check spam, if you don’t see it).

See you before the dust settles!

notes.title: Dustland: A Tale of Survival and Mystery in a Deserted Wasteland
notes.content:
The History
The land has become unrecognisable. Once fertile and lush land has become an endless expanse of sand, the sea that once dominated the view has dried up, and an endless scorching heat dominates the region.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/c221dec78c0bde713898e70b9c3363787946e60e.png

What happened? A cataclysm devastated the land. No one knows for sure what caused the cataclysm, some blame a military experiment gone wrong, while others whisper of mystical forces beyond the realm of human understanding. Whatever the cause, this part of the world - now known as Dustland - will never be the same.

The cataclysm that devastated the land came in three parts and by the time it subsided, only a lucky handful of people survived. First came the heat, with no warning, it took the people by surprise and many perished on the spot, some say they were the lucky ones. Next came a massive storm of biblical proportions lasting for days, the fury of the storm destroyed the few surviving surface structures, but that was not the worst part. With the storm came the monsters, a horrendous hoard of monstrous creatures. What are they and where did they come from? No one knows for sure, some bore the marks of human experiments gone wrong, while others "simply" looked more like terrifying aliens from another realm. Whatever the answers are, they were the final straw that turned the land into the wasteland that is now Dustland.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/4ddd14b5c8dd0cffe912cb26c0d76222b8e71156.png

Some people did survive the cataclysm, however, they now live day to day, fighting for simple survival. The worst part? Communication beyond the city is impossible, whether by radio or by attempting to travel through the desert, no one has made it out and no one has made it in. The survivors have no way of knowing if only their region has been devastated, or if they are the only survivors left on the planet. The rest of the world remains a mystery.

Survival in Dustland
In the ruins of a once-great city, survival is now the only goal. Sandstorms ravage the land, and monsters lurk beyond every corner. Amidst this chaos, the only refuge was the Shelter, a former seed vault that now houses the last remnants of humanity. But safety comes at a cost. Inside the Shelter, power is held by those who seem to know more about the cataclysm than they let on, and rumours about them run rampant. As for the normal survivors, they have split into factions, each vying for control and resources. At the bottom of the ladder are the unlucky ones, deemed to be expendable and sent out into the wasteland to scavenge for resources and face the dangers that lie beyond the shelter's walls.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/ede7b97de84867ce550be35a78c935ff3999da20.png

This is where you come in. After just barely making it into the Shelter, a burning desire for answers drives you forward. What really happened? Why did the region—or perhaps the world—fall into ruin?

notes.title: Dustland Playtest Recap and What’s Next
notes.content:
Hello there everyone,

The first stage of testing Dustland - our recent playtest session - was a fun one for everyone. We've had a while to look back at how things went and what we've learnt, and we'll be sharing that with you now, so join us as we go over what we've learnt!

Before anything, we want to thank everyone for taking part. We had hundreds of players dive into our post-apocalyptic world, and they hunted bugs, both the game enemy types and the bugs that we - the developers - need to squash!

All in all, this playtest was a crucial milestone for us as it allowed us to assess the game's mechanics and server performance under real-world conditions. As with all playtests for games at this early stage, there were many bumps on the road, but we learnt a lot of things that will shape the game's future direction.

Playtest Highlights
Player Participation
With hundreds of eager players taking part, we got a great first look at how the game would perform under multiplayer conditions. After all, it's one thing to develop a multiplayer game and test it internally, but it's an entirely different thing to let a few hundred players in at once.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/3817598293c3f822ab4d9bb273edd19ca8ae1f69.png

In-game, we saw that the players quickly passed through the tutorial, with a good split between those that played through the entire thing, and those that skipped the tutorial and went straight into the game. This tells us that having that skip option was a good choice.

Once in the main body of the game, we saw that the player took part in the main game's mission structure, with the in-game (enemy) bugs, being quickly hunted down.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44410666/e6b68c5f05f09ccb8b66a44eda7572fa050434a3.jpg

One point that we've learnt that will be important for future playtests is that we need to track the mission completions, so we'll be working on adding those tools so that we can closely monitor what the players do.

In-Game Combat
What about combat? Though it is early days, we did have various weapons in the game and it was clear to us that the players had no problem handling the enemies Dustland threw at them. Creatures that included swarms of bugs were eliminated throughout the test—an encouraging sign that players were adapting well to the game's combat mechanics. Perhaps, we could make things a little more challenging in the future!


Lessons Learned and Areas of Focus
Every playtest has a purpose, so what was the purpose of our playtest? We wanted to test the game's stability, find out how our servers performed under heavy load, and also, how the players interacted with the game's core mechanics.

So, what did we learn? As expected, there were some technical issues, such as server instability and bugs affecting mission mechanics. However, these are well within expectations, in fact, it would be much more concerning if no issues were found, especially at this very early stage.


 Server Stability: One of the primary objectives was to test server behaviour with a large number of concurrent players. While the servers performed well initially, as more players joined, the game's servers started to struggle, and even crash. For a playtest, this is great as we now know where we need to focus our efforts in order to improve the server stability.
 Mission Mechanics: We haven't reached concrete conclusions or decisions yet because we received a lot of feedback about how the missions work, but we will definitely be refining them.


What’s Next for Dustland?
Easy one first, we've begun working on fixing the critical bugs that were found during the playtest. These include server crashes, map-related issues, and inventory system problems.

Outside of the game, we'll be making improvements to the player registration systems, as it was clear that we need to make it easier for players to register and play the game.

Upcoming Playtest
Good news - the next playtest is scheduled for November 2024!

This next playtest will focus on refining the game’s stability and enhancing its core mechanics based on feedback from the initial playtest. You can expect smoother gameplay, better server performance, and much more polished mission structures as we continue to improve the game.

Finally, we'd like to once again thank everyone for taking part! This playtest also allowed us to begin forming the core of Dustland’s community as the level of engagement and feedback that we got was amazing. We can't wait for November and the second playtest when we show you the results of your feedback and our work!
